items.content_html:
This introduces a new package onlyoffice-desktopeditors-unwrapped, extracted from pkgs/by-name/on/onlyoffice-desktopeditors/package.nix. This allows users to use overrideAttrs on the unwrapped version of the package, and then pass it as an input to onlyoffice-desktopeditors.override.

Note, I'm not exactly sure what the convention for an -unwrapped package is, which hooks, if any, should be moved to pkgs/by-name/on/onlyoffice-desktopeditors/package.nix?

  • autoPatchelfHook
  • makeWrapper
  • wrapGAppsHook3

Also moved and updated update.sh, and made the script executable. While I was at it, I ran the script, so this PR also updates the package from 9.0.0 to 9.0.3.

Adds a refreshTimer option to disable fwupd-refresh.service and timer. The auto-refresh is useful on a server but not so much on a desktop, where the user is more to call fwupdmgr refresh and update themselves.

The refreshTimer is enabled by default for compatibility and as a good default. Feel free to close this if it is out of scope. Thank you!

items.content_html:
As discovered in #423212 (and fwupd#9014), there are two issues:

  1. The current implementation does not allow setting a user-defined value for services.fwupd.daemonSettings.EspLocation.
  2. fwupd does not accept trailing slashes in for the EspLocation option

This PR fixes (1) so far, I am happy to fix (2) too, but I am unsure how to do that yet, as my nix-foo is rather limited.

This fixes #423212

Things done

Add lib.mkDefault to line 187 to allow users to specify custom values for EspLocation.

items.title: tmuxPlugins.tmux-sessionx: 0-unstable-2024-09-22 -> 0-unstable-2025-01-07

items.content_html:
Description of changes

  • Adds tmux-window-name tmux plugin to tmuxPlugins.
  • This plugin automatically renames windows based on the active windows active process and/or current working directory.
  • This plugin requires interacting with the python libtmux, whose path is hardcoded into the shipped python scripts. So I did a few sed replacements in the postInstall step to patch for NixOS.
    • First, the entry file runs python3 -m pip list to check whether libtmux is available. This is handled by the wrapped script and its python env
    • Then, since its point is to check the running process and modify tmux window names to the respective applications, it required changes of the path it checks for the binaries, for example, to $HOME/.nix-profile/bin/* in a few places.
    • It does a good bit of regex replacement to get the active program, active path, etc. so those needed patching as well
